turns.content: Neutral-hydrogen clouds absorb quasar light at the Lyman-alpha rest wavelength of about 1216 Angstrom. Convert this to nanometres and determine whether the unredshifted line lies in the ground-accessible optical band.
Write the cosmological-redshift relation between rest and observed wavelength and rearrange it to solve for z.
Use 350 nm as an approximate blue cutoff for ground-based optical detection, and express this threshold in Angstrom so it can be compared with the stated rest wavelength.

Verify that the rest wavelength and adopted detection cutoff are valid wavelengths in compatible units. If they are, calculate the corresponding threshold value; otherwise leave the ratio unevaluated and identify the invalid input.
State the lower limit supported by the valid wavelength values currently available, or explain why it remains undetermined.
Explain how adopting a different practical cutoff or instrument-throughput criterion would shift the threshold.
Report the numerical lower limit and explain how the rest wavelength and observational cutoff determine it.
